stemMarkdown: The price of an article is first increased by 31%, and then the new price is decreased by 19%. What is the net percentage change in price? (Enter a negative value if it is a net decrease.)
solutionMarkdown: Take the original price as 100. After a 31% increase: $100 \times (1 + 31/100) = 131.00$. After a 19% decrease on 131.00: $131.00 \times (1 - 19/100) = 106.11$. Net change $= 106.11 - 100 = 6.11\%$.
altSolutionMarkdown: Shortcut formula: net \% change $= p_1 - p_2 - \dfrac{p_1 p_2}{100} = 31 - 19 - \dfrac{589}{100} = 6.11\%$.
